text:
Red squirrels are back in Wyrmwood. The first of them were released on 14 April 2024, when I stood at the edge of the reserve and watched small cages opened one by one beneath the pines.

In all, 48 red squirrels were let go across three sites in the reserve. Dr. Halvard Pemberton-Okoye, Lead Conservation Ecologist for the Wyrmwood Reserve Trust, oversaw the reintroduction and was on hand for the first release.

The full figures appear in the Wyrmwood Reintroduction Release Report, published by the Trust and presented at its annual public meeting. I was in the hall when it was discussed, and residents asked questions about the animals' future in the woodland.

Several locals told me they had not seen a red squirrel in the reserve in years. One walker said she planned to bring her grandchildren to look for them.
